title: Composite Signal Health Matrix and Auto-Notify for Cost/Latency Telemetry
creator: Ethan Park
description: Problem: Our current alerts are noisy and siloed per-metric (tokens, p99 latency, billing delta). Customers and SREs are repeatedly paged for symptoms without actionable triage guidance. We need a backend service that synthesizes multiple telemetry streams into a single 'signal health' score per customer/route/model, surfaces probable root causes, and drives fewer, higher-quality notifications.
proposal: Introduce a composite signal health matrix computed in the analytics pipeline that ingests existing cost/usage/latency timeseries and produces per-entity health vectors and a scalar health score. The service will run both online (near-real-time) detectors for acute degradation and a daily batch baseline job for drift/regression detection. Alerting will use severity buckets (INFO/SEV/CRIT), include contributory signal hints, and support automated suppression and escalation rules tied to customer tiers.
implementation_details: 1) Data pipeline: extend the hourly ingestion job to emit normalized metrics (z-score, seasonality flags) into a new telemetry.partitioned_signals table. 2) Detection: ensemble approach: short-window change-point detectors (robust CUSUM), STL-based seasonality-aware residuals, and a light-weight forecasting residual model (exponential smoothing) for baseline deviations. 3) Scoring: combine standardized residuals with weight profiles per-metric to compute a composite health score; store per-step at 1m granularity for 48h. 4) Explainability: attach top-3 contributing metrics and a short natural-language hint (e.g., "latency rise concentrated on eu-west, correlated with model x kv-cache miss rate") using correlated-delta heuristics. 5) Alerting: create AlertPolicy resources in the console backend that map score thresholds to channels (email, slack, pagerduty) with per-customer overrides and throttling. 6) Rollout: start with internal customers and opt-in beta for high-usage customers before broad release.
data_migration: Create new partitioned_signals table and backfill 90 days from raw telemetry. Provide a migration job that marks legacy alerts as superseded. Backfill will be throttled to avoid overwhelming query cluster.
tradeoffs_and_risks:
- Ensemble detectors reduce false positives but increase compute; mitigate by adaptive sampling and heavier weight on cheap detectors.
- Explainability heuristics are heuristic and may mislead triage; expose confidence and link to raw traces/dashboards.
- Per-customer weighting increases complexity; default weight profile will be used initially with admin override UI later.
observability_and_telemetry: Instrument end-to-end latency for the detection pipeline, compute cost impact estimate (USD/day) for running online detectors, and add internal dashboards showing alert volume, suppression rate, and mean time to acknowledge (MTTA).
testing_plan: Unit tests for detector components, integration tests with synthetic injected degradations, e2e canary for a single high-usage account with manual on-call monitoring for 72 hours, and chaos test to ensure suppression rules behave under upstream metric flaps.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Internal preview (ENG+SRE) 2 weeks. Phase 1: Beta with 5 opt-in customers 3 weeks. Phase 2: Gradual ramp to 50% of tenants over 4 weeks with monitoring gates. Final: full release in console-2025.03 if gates pass.
acceptance_criteria: Composite health score computed and stored at 1m granularity for internal tenants
False-positive rate reduced by >=30% on sampled historical incidents compared to current rule-based alerts
Alert payloads include top-3 contributing metrics and a dashboard link
Throttling/suppression prevents more than one active alert per entity per 15 minutes by default
Cost for running online detectors remains within budgeted estimate (<$150/day initially)
